transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Ever since that robbery a couple of years ago, I keep organizing my whole life around avoiding anything that reminds me of it—certain neighborhoods, late meetings, even some community events. It has gotten to the point where I'm arranging my entire schedule just to avoid feeling unsafe, and I realized I can't keep living like this.
Do memories of the robbery ever come back in unwanted ways, like nightmares, flashbacks, or feeling as if it’s happening again? If so, how often does that happen?

Yes, out of nowhere—like when I'm locking up an office—I'll suddenly see myself back on that floor with the gun at my head, and it feels so real that my chest tightens and I can't breathe. Other nights, I lie awake for hours replaying it, and when I do sleep, I often wake up with my heart racing.
During the robbery, did you believe you might be killed or seriously injured, or see someone else threatened that way? How intense was your fear or helplessness in that moment?

Yes, I absolutely believed we were going to die. I was forced at gunpoint to lie on the floor while one of our younger employees was pistol-whipped right next to me. The fear and helplessness were completely overwhelming because I genuinely thought either he or I would be killed right then and there.

Since the robbery, have you noticed lasting changes in how you think or feel, like blaming yourself or others, feeling detached from people, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy? If so, which of these has been the biggest problem for you?

I struggle with all of those—I blame myself for being there so late, feel like the world is no longer safe, and feel completely detached from my family and church, like I'm watching them behind glass. Things I used to love, like salsa class or taking my granddaughter to the museum, now feel completely flat. Honestly, feeling so disconnected and detached from the people I love has been the hardest part of all.
Since the robbery, have you been constantly on guard or easily startled, like jumping at noises or always scanning for danger? Has this been happening most days?

Yes, absolutely. I'm constantly scanning for exits and watching who comes and goes, which makes it impossible to relax. If a car door slams or someone walks up behind me, I jump out of my skin and my heart races, and this has been happening pretty much every day for well over a year.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a qualifying traumatic event involving threatened death and witnessing severe violence, followed by persistent re-experiencing, marked avoidance, negative alterations in cognition and mood, and hyperarousal symptoms lasting well over one year with clear functional impairment in daily scheduling, relationships, and activities. This pattern is most consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder.
